one_sentence_story: Darley and Latané proved in 1968 that decent people bolt to help 85 percent of the time when they know they are the ONLY witness, yet drop to 31 percent when they think four others are listening — because shared responsibility feels like someone else's job.
so_what_for_you: Never shout 'Somebody help!' or CC ten people on an urgent task; point to one specific person by name or clothing to turn a frozen crowd back into an 85-percent responder.

jargon_map.plain: each witness feeling less personal duty to act as the number of other witnesses grows
jargon_map.analogy: like five roommates all assuming someone else took out the trash

jargon_map.plain: everyone privately worrying something is wrong while acting calm, convincing each other nothing is wrong
jargon_map.analogy: like twenty students confused by a lecture who all nod because nobody raises a hand

jargon_map.plain: lower individual probability and slower speed of helping when passive others are present
jargon_map.analogy: like cars driving past a stranded motorist on a busy highway faster than on a country lane

jargon_map.plain: singling out one specific individual to break diffusion of responsibility
jargon_map.analogy: like handing the relay baton into one runner's palm
